anchors: re-Read it before the next Edit of that table
decision: After the reformat hook realigns a table, re-Read the rows before the next Edit of that table.

evidence.text: Seen in this session: a Rust table cell edit realigned 15 rows of the table. GREEN opus and haiku re-Read before the second edit.

reopen_if: The hook stops realigning on Write/Edit, or Edit starts matching whitespace-insensitively.
why: Realigning rewrites every row's padding, so an old_string copied from an earlier Read fails 'String to replace not found'; a public install has no memory line saying so.

anchors: write every content row with one space either side of each cell and no padding
decision: A table whose widest row, padded per rule 1, would run past 300 display columns is written compact: one space either side of each cell, no padding, separator cells --- touching the pipes with their colons kept.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-26 (cap in the formatter, then split compuse-toolbox); token cost measured 2026-11-26 with claude -p on opus and haiku

reopen_if: Claude Code or the model tokenizer makes runs of spaces near free (re-measure padded vs unpadded tokens), or a reader needs wide tables aligned in the raw file.
why: Padding a column to one long cell repeats that width on every row; in compuse-toolbox one 6,382-character cell made 308 of the SKILL.md's 409 KB spaces, 19.3k of its 54.8k tokens per invocation on opus. Rows past 300 columns overflow any editor line, so aligning them buys nothing.
